§7.6 rule (b) (S483 q8-fu2) — `${ const c: number = n % v(2); }` inside `

5)>`, `v` a recursive function the compiler types only in part: the divisor is not proven a `number`, so the `%` may be between `int`s by 0 — E-FILE-SCOPE-INIT-IN-CONSTRUCT.
rationale: §7.6 rule (b) (S483 q8-fu2): a `%` is a trap site when neither operand is proven a `number` on every branch and the divisor is not proven non-zero; an operand with a branch the compiler could not type is not proven (#2133 review LOW-1 — fail closed). ruling:user-voice-scrml.md-S483-q8-division: "inside a construct refuse only what can actually trap: keep `%` and integer division by a possibly-zero int refused".
